title: Ban Chiang potters decorate a jar with red designs
summary: A jar associated with the Ban Chiang tradition combines a buff surface with red painted decoration, showing a distinctive approach to earthenware design.

citations.locator: Object 1987.424.9; Date, Medium and painted decoration; phase-label inconsistency retained

claims.text: A jar associated with the Ban Chiang tradition combines a buff surface with red painted decoration, showing a distinctive approach to earthenware design.
The Met’s Date field gives 300 BCE–200 CE. Its “Middle period” label conflicts with the description’s final-phase association; broader archaeological dating remains unresolved.
The record concerns this catalogued object. Its phase label and descriptive chronology are inconsistent, so it is not used to date all Ban Chiang pottery.
